name: Zambia
summary: There is no forced heirship: the Wills and Administration of Testate Estates Act 1989 lets a person make a will, and dependants may seek financial provision from the estate. The Intestate Succession Act 1989 governs estates without a will. Trusts and foundations were not sourced.
family_claims: Wills and Administration of Testate Estates Act 1989 (Cap. 60) lets dependants seek financial provision. Intestate Succession Act 1989 (Cap. 59) gives spouse, children, dependants and relatives set shares.
foreign_law_note: The Intestate Succession Act applies to persons domiciled in Zambia and members of customary communities; no source on foreign law.
trust_note: Trusts: not sourced; 'yes' assumes common-law trusts; unverified. No private-foundation law found.
open_questions: A 2017 family provision statute was suggested but not confirmed.
Trust law and foundations not sourced.

Hague Trusts Convention: The HCCH status table (checked 2026-10-16) lists 14 Contracting Parties; this country is not one of them and no UK, Dutch or Chinese extension covers it, so the 1985 Convention is not in force here.
Domestic trusts: likely available under the inherited common-law or Roman-Dutch tradition, but no statute or official source was read; confirm before marking yes.
